why: A singleton cubit keeps the previous screen's state and emits after close(). Cubits are always registerFactory.

easy_localization re-exports package:intl, whose TextDirection is a class with LTR/RTL constants - not the dart:ui enum with .ltr/.rtl that Text.textDirection takes. Any widget file that both imports easy_localization and pins text direction (needed whenever English words sit in an Arabic-first UI) fails to compile until intl's version is hidden.

topic: cubit with several repos: named initializing formals, public fields
why: Dart forbids named parameters that start with an underscore, so `required this._progressRepo` will not compile and the private-field + initializer-list form trips prefer_initializing_formals. For a single dependency keep the house positional form `Cubit(this._repo)`; once there are two or more, name them and make the fields public - which also matches the golden ArchiveCubit pattern where the repo field is public and injectable in tests.

topic: presentation-only features legitimately have no data/ folder (R12)
why: R12 flags a missing data/ folder as a warning, not an error, precisely because it cannot tell an incomplete feature from a presentation-only one. When several screens read the same tables, one data-owning feature plus injected repos keeps `fromJson`/error mapping in a single place; duplicating a data layer per screen is the actual violation. Confirm and move on rather than scaffolding empty folders.

topic: CrossAxisAlignment.stretch on a Row inside a vertical ListView
why: In a vertical ListView every child is laid out with maxHeight: infinity. RenderFlex with CrossAxisAlignment.stretch passes BoxConstraints.tightFor(height: constraints.maxHeight) to each child, so the children get a tight infinite height and layout throws; the subtree is then left unsized and the next pointer event fails with "Cannot hit test a render box with no size". IntrinsicHeight resolves the row to the tallest child's intrinsic height first, which keeps the equal-height look that stretch was there for (needed because translated labels wrap to two lines in Arabic but one in English). This is the same family as the house rule "never Expanded in an unconstrained scrollable" — stretch on the cross axis is the vertical twin of it. flutter analyze cannot catch this: it is a layout-time error only.

topic: R10 fires on Expanded and SingleChildScrollView in exclusive branches
wrong:
// "Fixing" an R10 warning by removing a correct Expanded, or by wrapping the
// bounded Row in a SizedBox with a guessed height.
why: The real rule is that Expanded must not be a direct child of an unbounded scrollable. A Row's Expanded constrains width, which is bounded by the parent Column, so it is always safe; and a scroll view nested inside an Expanded is the standard way to give a scrollable bounded space. Checking the actual parent chain takes a moment and saves breaking working layout. Contrast with the genuine violation recorded for CrossAxisAlignment.stretch on a Row inside a vertical ListView, which flutter_check does not catch at all.

topic: stretch Row inside a scrollable needs IntrinsicHeight
why: On a Row, CrossAxisAlignment.stretch is vertical: the Row hands each child a tight height equal to its own. A direct child of a vertical ListView (or any scrollable) gets maxHeight: infinity, so there is no finite height to stretch to and the children are never laid out. IntrinsicHeight bounds the Row to the tallest child's intrinsic height, which both fixes the crash and keeps the equal-height cards that stretch was there for. Note this is a latent crash: it only fires once the screen's cubit reaches success and actually renders the row, so a screen stuck on an error or skeleton state hides it. In this project the same three-stat row exists in home, profile and progress; home had the IntrinsicHeight and the other two did not. When fixing one, grep `CrossAxisAlignment.stretch` across lib/ and check every hit whose parent is a Row (Column + stretch is horizontal and safe inside a bounded-width parent).

topic: create or replace view only accepts columns appended last
right:
-- Start from the LATEST definition of the view (0005, not 0001) and append:
create or replace view public.word_overview
with (security_invoker = on) as
select
  ...                                   -- every existing column, same order
  (f.word_id is not null) as is_favorite,
  coalesce((select array_agg(i.list_id ...)), '{}'::text[]) as list_ids,
  w.field_id,                           -- new columns go last
  fl.name_en as field_name_en,
  fl.color   as field_color
from public.words w
join public.categories c on c.id = w.category_id
left join public.fields fl on fl.id = w.field_id
...;

-- A dependent view that used `w.*` expanded it at definition time, so it does
-- NOT inherit the new columns: replace it too, with the same body.
create or replace view public.word_list_entries ... select i.list_id, w.* ...;
wrong:
-- Re-stating word_overview from 0001 and slotting the new column in where it
-- belongs logically. Two separate failures:
create or replace view public.word_overview as
select
  w.id,
  w.category_id,
  w.field_id,            -- inserted mid-list -> 42P16 cannot change name of
  w.word,                --   view column "field_id" to "word"
  ...
  (f.word_id is not null) as is_favorite
  -- and `list_ids`, added by 0005, silently dropped -> the word-list chips
  --   stop rendering because WordModel.listIds is always empty
from public.words w ...
why: Postgres allows `create or replace view` to add trailing columns and nothing else — reordering, renaming or dropping one raises 42P16 on an applied database, and a column quietly left out breaks every client that reads it. Because each migration re-states the whole view, the one to copy from is the most recent migration that touched it, never 0001. Check which migrations redefine the view (`grep -l word_overview supabase/migrations/`) before writing a new one. The same applies to views built on it: `w.*` is expanded and frozen at creation, so a dependent view needs its own create-or-replace to pick the new columns up.

topic: RLS `to authenticated` on a table a pre-auth screen reads
wrong:
-- Copied from `categories_read` without checking WHO reads the table.
create policy fields_read on public.fields
  for select to authenticated using (true);

-- The field picker is a step on the REGISTER screen, so it runs as `anon`.
-- The anon role passes the policy and sees zero rows: the query SUCCEEDS,
-- so the UI shows its empty state ("no fields set up yet"), not its error
-- state. Nothing is logged and nothing is thrown.
why: Empty state vs error state is the diagnostic: an unapplied migration or a missing grant raises a PostgrestException that ErrorMapper turns into a failure state with a Retry button, while an RLS policy that excludes the caller returns an empty result set and renders the empty state instead. So "no rows, no error" on a freshly added table means the policy does not cover the role actually asking — check whether the screen runs before or after sign-in before copying a policy from another table. The second half matters just as much: a required form input backed by a list that can legitimately come back empty locks the user out of the screen entirely, so make it optional and enforce it somewhere a skip is possible. Same family as the skip guard on the choose-field redirect.

topic: scope a whole app by putting the filter in the view, not every query
why: A per-query filter is only as good as the next developer's memory, and it cannot cover views built on views: `word_list_entries` selects from `word_overview`, so a predicate inside `word_overview` reaches it for free while a client-side `.eq()` never would. Keeping the "no value = unrestricted" branch is what lets legacy rows and an un-set profile keep working instead of seeing an empty app. The cost is that the filter is invisible at the call site, so it must be stated in the view's comment AND the data source's class doc; leave any explicit `.eq(...)` that already exists in place, since it still helps the planner use the index and tells the reader what the query means.
